messages.subject: Question about occupancy simulation in AHM book
parts:
Dear list members,

In pages 585 and 586 of the AHM book there is a script tu run a simulation for a simple static occupancy model.

The 4th line

estimates <- array(dim = c(2,simreps,3,3))

1) What the "2" means in the script?

2) After the simulation, how can I calculate the RMSE similar to the ones that appears in the table 10.2?

Best,

Manuel

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Question about occupancy simulation in AHM book
parts:
Dear Manuel,

well, the 2 is the first dimension of the array named "estimates". Lower down, we save the coeffients of the model and there are two of them:

      estimates[,i,j,k] <- coef(tmp)


Then, to calculate the RMSE, you can use this code for the specific case of our simulation. This assumes that true psi is 0.5 and you may have to adapt this for your case.

Best regards  --  Marc



# Compute % root mean square error for each of the nine scenarios

 

for(j in 1:3){

  for(k in 1:3){

    lab <- paste(nsites[j],"sites,", nsurveys[k],"surveys")

#    cat(lab)

    rmse <- sqrt(mean((plogis(estimates[1,,j,k]) - 0.5)^2)) # RMSE

#    mean(sqrt((plogis(estimates[1,,j,k]) - 0.5)^2)) # mean root squared error

    perc.rmse <- 100 * (rmse / 0.5)

  cat(paste("\n***", lab,":", round(perc.rmse, 0), "***"))

}

}

messages.subject: RE: Question about occupancy simulation in AHM book
parts:
Dear Manuel,

the model has two coefficients, one intercept for psi and another one for p. I save both, but, true, only use one of them afterwards. So yes, you could drop that dimension of the results array and directly only save the first coefficient (which I think is the intercept for psi).

Best regards  --- Marc
